landmarks.name: Hagia Sophia
landmarks.writeup: A historic architectural marvel in Istanbul, originally a cathedral, later a mosque, and now a museum.

wiki.extract: Hagia Sophia mosque in İznik (Nicaea) in Bursa Province, Turkey, was built as a Byzantine-era basilican church. Converted into the Orhan Mosque after the Ottoman conquest, it was turned into a museum in 1935. The church is now once again in service as a mosque. It is in the town centre of İznik, within the old walled area.

landmarks.name: Cappadocia
landmarks.writeup: Famous for its unique rock formations, cave dwellings, and hot air balloon rides.

wiki.extract: Cappadocia is a historical region in Central Anatolia region, Turkey. It is largely in the provinces of Nevşehir, Kayseri, Aksaray, Kırşehir, Sivas and Niğde. Today, the touristic Cappadocia Region is located in Nevşehir province.

landmarks.name: Topkapi Palace
landmarks.writeup: The former palace of Ottoman sultans, located in Istanbul, showcasing imperial collections.

wiki.extract: The Topkapı Palace or the Seraglio, is a large museum and library in the east of the Fatih district of Istanbul in Turkey. From the 1460s to the completion of Dolmabahçe Palace in 1853, it served as the administrative center of the Ottoman Empire, and was the main residence of its sultans.

landmarks.name: Pamukkale
landmarks.writeup: Known for its white travertine terraces and thermal waters.

wiki.extract: Pamukkale, meaning "cotton castle" in Turkish, is a natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey. The area is famous for a carbonate mineral left by the flowing of thermal spring water. It is located in Turkey's Inner Aegean region, in the River Menderes valley, which has a temperate climate for most of the year.

landmarks.name: Ephesus
landmarks.writeup: Ancient Greco-Roman city with well-preserved ruins including the Library of Celsus.

wiki.extract: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Ionia, in present-day Selçuk in İzmir Province, Turkey. It was built in the 10th century BC on the site of Apasa, a city-state that was also the capital of Arzawa, by Attic and Ionian Greek colonists. During the Classical Greek era, it was one of twelve cities that were members of the Ionian League. The city came under the control of the Roman Republic in 129 BC.

cultural_events.name: Whirling Dervishes Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A spiritual Sufi ceremony featuring the famous spinning dance, held annually in Konya.

wiki.extract: Sufi whirling is a form of physically active meditation which originated among certain Sufi groups, and which is still practiced by the Sufi dervishes of the Mevlevi order and other orders such as the Rifa'i-Marufi. It is a customary meditation practice performed within the sema, or worship ceremony, through which dervishes aim to reach greater connection with Allah. This is sought through abandoning one's nafs, ego or personal desires, by listening to the music, focusing on God, and spinning one's body in repetitive circles, which has been seen as a symbolic imitation of planets in the Solar System orbiting the Sun.

cultural_events.name: Istanbul Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An international film festival showcasing global and Turkish cinema.

wiki.extract: The Istanbul Film Festival is the first and oldest international film festival in Turkey, organised by the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts. It is held every year in April in movie theaters in Istanbul, Turkey. As mentioned in its regulations, the festival aims to encourage the development of cinema in Turkey and to promote films of quality in the Turkish cinema market.

cultural_events.name: Oil Wrestling Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Traditional Turkish wrestling event held in Edirne, known as one of the oldest sports festivals.

wiki.extract: Oil wrestling, also called Turkish oil wrestling, is the national sport of Turkey. Oil wrestling includes oil and traditional dress, and its rules are comparable to karakucak.

food_writeup: Turkish cuisine is rich and diverse, featuring dishes like kebabs, mezes, baklava, and Turkish tea, blending Middle Eastern, Mediterranean, and Central Asian flavors.
brief_history: Turkey, historically known as Anatolia, has been home to ancient civilizations including the Hittites, Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, and Ottomans. The Republic of Turkey was founded in 1923 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk following the fall of the Ottoman Empire.
current_conflicts: Turkey is involved in regional conflicts including tensions in Syria, disputes over Cyprus, and issues related to Kurdish groups.

commentary.inflation_management: Turkey is the textbook case of unorthodox monetary policy's costs. Inflation was 6.2% in 2009 (the low), 12.3% in 2020, then exploded to 72.3% in 2022, the series high, after the central bank cut rates into rising inflation on political direction — the lira collapsed. It was still 58.5% in 2024 and is projected at 34.9% for 2025: disinflation under the post-2023 orthodox turn (aggressive hikes under a new economic team), but far from target. Central-bank independence was effectively suspended 2018-23; credibility is being rebuilt but the 2022-24 episode destroyed years of anchoring.
commentary.debt_management: Turkey's public debt is low and falling: 44.2% of GDP in 2006 (the series high), 38.3% in 2020, 29.4% in 2022, and a projected series low of 23.5% in 2025. The paradox is that low sovereign debt coexists with chronic macro instability — the vulnerabilities are private-sector FX debt, the current account, and inflation, not the sovereign balance sheet. GDP grew from $554.9bn in 2006 to a projected $1,597.3bn in 2025. The state's borrowing is modest; the risk is that a currency crisis forces contingent liabilities onto the sovereign, as quasi-fiscal schemes (like the FX-protected deposit program) have done.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis; Turkey recovered fast on credit-fueled growth.
Lira crisis (2018): the currency collapsed as the central bank resisted hiking; inflation took off.
Unorthodox policy experiment: rate cuts into 70%+ inflation (2021-23) produced the 72.3% peak in 2022.
Orthodox turn (mid-2023): new economic team hiked rates aggressively; disinflation began.
Inflation projected at 34.9% — falling but still the highest in the G20; debt at a series low of 23.5% of GDP.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Turkey's outlook hinges on whether the orthodox turn holds through the political cycle: disinflation from 72.3% to a projected 34.9% is real progress, but credibility is fragile and the 2028 election cycle is the test. The structural vulnerabilities — energy import dependence, private FX debt, the current-account deficit — are unchanged. Low public debt is a genuine buffer. The honest analytical assessment: the direction is right, the destination (single-digit inflation) is years away, and political risk is the dominant variable.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
